item.title: Gifu Events 2026: Takayama Festival, Gujo Odori & Cormorant Fishing
item.description: Gifu’s mountainous heart hosts some of Japan’s most refined and enduring traditions. The Takayama Festival’s ornate automaton floats are counted among the country’s most beautiful; Gujo Odori is a dance the whole town joins for two months, culminating in four all-night sessions; and on the Nagara River, cormorant fishing has continued unbroken for 1,300 years. Add the winter magic of Shirakawa-go’s illuminated thatched village, and Gifu rewards a well-timed 2026 trip.

item.title: Gujo Odori: Japan's Longest Summer Dance Festival — Guide
item.description: Gujo Odori is one of Japan’s three great folk dances and one of its longest-running summer festivals, held over roughly 30 nights across the summer in the water town of Gujo Hachiman. Unlike festivals watched from the sidelines, Gujo Odori is a participatory dance in which anyone, locals and visitors alike, joins the circle around a central stage to dance to live music and singing, and during the famous Obon period in mid-August the celebration continues in all-night dances that run until dawn.
